 "architecture": "TypeScript on Node 24, zero dependencies, about 900 lines of brain plus a world model (terrain, 259 prisms in a 16 m hash, shot and sight rays, tree occlusion), a 2 m walk grid with A*, one flat parameter table, a fuzz test (10,000 random observations must never throw), and a dev-only simulator. Entry point wraps the brain in try/catch; fallback walks toward the next zone centre and does not fire.\n\nDecision structure is a strict priority ladder evaluated fresh every decision (no utility blending), with one piece of hysteresis (the previous mode name):\n1. Zone: if outside the circle (or within 3 m of its edge), or if straight-line distance to a ring at 70% of the next radius, times 1.4, divided by walk speed, plus 8 s slack, exceeds the time left until the shrink ends. Boosts, still shoots targets of opportunity.\n2. Fight: a mech is currently visible and HP fraction is at least 40%, plus 15 points per additional hostile that has a clear shot line on us, and at least 75% if three or more mechs are in view within 220 m.\n3. Retreat: a target is visible or we were hit in the last 4 s, and we fail the fight test. Runs (boosting) to a cover point while still aiming and shooting at the target, so the front stays toward the threat.\n4. Regen: entered only after retreat; stand still facing the last hit direction until 85% HP. While in it a visible hunter is ignored until it actually hits us.\n5. Roam, sub-priorities in order: visible cube within 90 m; weapon pickup within 25 m; supply drop; weapon pickup within 170 m; NPC drone within 170 m; crate within 90 m with a line of fire; rotate to the 70% ring of the next circle; otherwise hold beside a wall.\nAlways-on layers after mode choice: projectile/laser dodge vector added at 1.6 weight, stuck recovery, boost hysteresis (on above 55 energy, off below 25), aim and fire, pickup handling, upgrade pick.\nMemory: mech and drone tracks kept 12 s, but only tracks seen in the last 0.3 s count as hostiles for targeting; tracks up to 5 s old count as threats for cover and peek searches. Free-for-all mode is auto-detected when more mechs have died than our kills plus one; it only switches off drone farming while hostiles are near.\nCPU budget: at most one A* per decision and only if under 12 ms of wall time has been used; cover and peek searches consider the 4 nearest threats. Reported p99 about 4-5 ms in Docker.",
 "navigation": "Ground-only 2 m grid built at start-up. Each cell stores the standing surface (terrain, or a prism top when the prism underside is lower than one mech height above ground), a roof flag (prism top more than step height above ground), and a wall flag (any of the 8 neighbours cannot be stepped to). A step is allowed if the rise is at most the step-up height, or neither cell is a roof and the slope is within about 90% of the 50 degree limit; drops are always allowed, so walking off ledges is permitted one-way.\nSearch is weighted A* (octile heuristic inflated 1.3x), 8-connected with no corner cutting, cells next to walls cost 3.5x, cap 25,000 expansions, returns the path to the closest reached cell when the cap or an unreachable goal stops it. Goals are snapped to the nearest cell of the bot's own connected region (regions are 4-connected, both-direction walkable components, sized at build time).\nPath following: replan when the goal moves more than 6 m, every 3 s, or when more than 8 m off the path; steer at the farthest of the next 10 path cells reachable by a straight walkable line that does not touch wall-adjacent cells. If no A* budget is available it just steers straight at the goal.\nReachability gate: cubes, weapons, drops must be in the bot's own region; pickups sitting on roofs are skipped.\nJets and roofs: no deliberate roof play at all; roof cells are excluded from cover, peek and camp spots. Jets are used only (a) in stuck recovery and (b) to escape a 'pocket': when the bot's region has fewer than 3000 cells (about 12,000 square metres) and the goal is outside it, it walks straight at the goal, jumps whenever grounded and jets while energy is above 5. This was added after a real zone death from following a zone goal into a sealed courtyard.\nStuck handling: if movement was commanded for 1.1 s but displacement was under 1 m, jump and boost for 0.6 s; on every second stuck event the next path cell is blacklisted for 20 s and a replan is forced.\nBoost: used when the goal is over 50 m away, and always in zone, retreat and drop modes, subject to the 55/25 energy hysteresis.",
 "aiming_and_fire_control": "Target point is the body centre (half height, scaled by the target's cube count). One 'primary' weapon decides the commanded aim each decision, chosen in this order: lightning if within 95% of its range with line of fire and energy for two shots; else laser if within 97% of range, line of fire, and its cooldown is under 0.4 s or it is already charging; else gun within 95% of range with line of fire; else mortar between 22 m and 230 m.\nGun: lead from the closed-form constant-velocity intercept time (falls back to distance over bullet speed), ignoring the target's vertical velocity for mechs. The gun fires independently of which weapon is primary whenever the current slewed aim is within the angular size of 75% of the target radius plus half the spread angle of the gun's own lead solution, with ammo left. No check that the lead point itself is unobstructed.\nLaser: starts charging when cooldown is zero, line of fire exists and aim error is under 0.25 rad; holds until the charge is within 0.05 s of full AND the aim is on the centre within the target's angular radius, then releases. Never fires partial charges. If line of fire is lost it keeps holding for up to 2.5 s before letting go. No lead (hitscan). The half-speed penalty while charging is not compensated in movement.\nLightning: fires when the yaw error is inside 70% of the half-cone.\nMortar: low arc with line of sight, high arc without; three fixed-point iterations of flight-time lead; fires only when aim error is under 0.02 rad. Because it is last in the primary order it is effectively an indirect-fire tool for when nothing else can shoot.\nTarget selection (lower is better): 0.6 x distance plus 0.15 x target HP, minus 120 for a clear line of fire, minus 40 if it hit us in the last 3 s, minus 60 for being the current target with line of fire. The stated purpose is focus fire: damage spread over several hunters is wasted because they regenerate.\nReload policy: only when no fight target, reload early if the magazine is under half. No tactical reload behind cover during fights.\nWith no target: face the last hit bearing for 3 s, else a recent non-far sound bearing (2 s), else sweep the torso plus or minus about 1.2 rad around the heading; when standing still, spin slowly to scan.",
 "survival_and_anti_squad_tactics": "Core doctrine reached after their ablations: in practice mode points equal house bots dead before us, so kills bank points and time spent hiding or standing still only lets hunters gather and regenerate. Passive changes lost about 0.45 twice.\nFighting the hunters: keep a stand-off range by weapon (gun 75 m in every scored build, 100 m in the unscored HEAD; laser 120 m; mortar-only 110 m; lightning 28 m when the target is within 70 m, is not a mech, or no laser is held; at least 50 m from drones; 20-40 m from crates). Movement is a radial term proportional to range error over 25 m plus a 0.9 tangential strafe whose direction flips at random every 0.6-1.8 s and flips when the next 4 m would hit a wall.\nPeek spots (their main anti-squad device): every 0.5 s, when other hostiles are tracked, sample 4 rings (6, 12, 20, 30 m) of 12 points; a point needs a line of fire to the chosen target, pays 100 per other tracked hostile (4 nearest, up to 5 s old) with a shot line to our body, plus small costs for range error and travel; move only if it beats the current spot by 20. Result: fight one hunter from a spot the others cannot shoot.\nRetreat threshold scales with exposure: 40% HP alone, 55% with two shooters, 70% with three, and 75% whenever three or more mechs are in view.\nCover search on retreat: 5 rings (8 to 56 m) of 16 points; cost is ring radius plus 200 per threat with a clear shot line plus 0.8 per metre moved toward any threat; must stay inside the current or next circle; walls count as cover, trees do not (trees block sight but not shots, and hunters remember us for 5 s). If nothing is hidden, run 40 m directly away from the threats with a half-weight pull toward the next circle. Recomputed once a second.\nRegen cycle: after a retreat, stand still (silent) until 85% HP, then resume. They established from the rules that regen (45 HP/s after 5 s without dealing or taking damage) runs while moving too, so standing still buys only silence.\nDodging: sidestep any visible bullet whose closest approach in the next 0.8 s is within 4.5 m; leave the predicted landing point of visible mortar shells (splash radius plus 3.5 m, up to 4 s ahead); sidestep when a visible mech is charging a laser with its yaw within a 6 m lateral window of us.\nDrones that shoot us while no mech is in view are killed rather than tanked.\nNo explicit plan for the single early hunter beyond the normal fight mode, no kiting toward terrain choke points, no late-game plan for when all 15 hunt; their notes say their sim bot dies at about 99 s on average.",
 "loot_weapons_upgrades": "Weapon values used for loadout decisions: laser 3, lightning 2.6, gun 1.6, mortar 1.2; a swap needs a gain of at least 0.4; duplicates are never held; the lower-valued slot is dropped; no swapping while a laser is charging. Net effect: the bot ends on laser plus lightning and gives up the gun when it finds both. Pickups are sought within 170 m (value falls with distance, scale 50 m), must be reachable on foot and not on a roof.\nThe alternative loadout that valued the gun above lightning (laser 3, gun 2, lightning 1.3, mortar 1) was only ever scored inside the seven-change bundle that lost 0.46, so it is unresolved.\nUpgrades, fixed preference order: plating, armor, nanites, laser damage, lightning efficiency, gun damage, laser charge, gun rate, lightning range, gyros, lightning chain, gun velocity, gun magazine, mortar reload, servos, capacitor, reactor, jets, sensors, laser pierce, mortar splash, mortar velocity. Rationale given: plating multiplies max HP by 1.15 per stack versus about 1.087 effective HP for armor, and armor does not reduce zone damage, which decides late deaths.\nCubes: walk to any visible reachable cube within 90 m as the top roam priority; during a fight grab cubes within 30 m if above the retreat HP.\nCrates: shoot crates within 90 m that have a line of fire, standing 20-40 m away, only above 60% HP and before 330 s.\nDrones: shoot drones within 170 m under the same HP and time gates, from at least 50 m.\nSupply drops: go (boosting) if no mech is in view within 220 m, the drop is within 300 m, nobody else holds it, it is reachable, and straight-line walking time is no more than time-to-landing plus 6 s.  "zone_and_endgame": "Rotation target is a point on the ring at 70% of the next radius along the line from the next centre to the bot. It becomes the top priority only when outside or when the arrival-time test (straight-line distance x 1.4 at walk speed plus 8 s) would miss the end of the shrink; otherwise rotating is the second-lowest roam activity. Cover points and hold spots must lie inside the current or next circle.\nIdle state is 'hold': nearest wall-adjacent, non-roof ground cell within 24 m that is inside the 70% ring of the next circle, re-chosen every 15 s, approached slowly.\nNo dedicated endgame logic. Farming stops at 330 s. Their written analysis: the final circle reaches radius 0 at about 415 s at 260 HP/s, before the 480 s cap, so a match can never end on the clock; a late game ends in zone deaths ordered mainly by current HP, which armor and regen cannot help, hence max-HP (plating, cubes) is what matters late. They estimate max achievable HP at about 2981 (10 cubes, 3 plating). Their sim logs 2-4 zone deaths per 96 matches, so the rotation timing is not fully safe.",

 "novel_ideas": [
  "Treat the practice scorer as an exact A/B instrument: fixed seeds mean one single-parameter change per submission gives a clean delta; never stack changes (their two stacked submissions were uninterpretable) and never spend a submission on a replicate once determinism is known.",
  "Scoring identity for practice mode: points = house bots dead before us. Kills bank points immediately; survival time is worth something only through later kills or other house deaths (zone, drones, own mortar splash).",
  "Passivity is measurably bad: standing still to regen or hiding behind trees cost about 0.45 each time. Regen runs while moving, so keep moving and working (looting, repositioning) during the 5 s no-damage window instead of standing still.",
  "Peek-spot fighting: pick a position with a line of fire to the one chosen target that the other tracked hunters cannot shoot, re-evaluated twice a second. This is a cheap way to turn a squad fight into serial duels.",
  "Exposure-scaled disengage: raise the retreat HP threshold by a fixed step for every additional enemy with a clear shot line, plus a separate high threshold when three or more are in view.",
  "Focus-fire scoring with stickiness and low-HP preference, motivated by enemy regen making spread damage worthless.",
  "Free-for-all auto-detection: if more mechs have died than we killed plus one, the opponents are fighting each other, so this is not the squad mode. A one-line mode switch usable for the finals.",
  "Pocket escape: connected-component size as a detector for sealed courtyards, with jet-over-the-wall as the exit.",
  "Supply drops as the only farming change that paid: extend the chase distance for drops that are still falling (3 cubes plus full heal), but do not divert to drops that have already landed far away.",
  "Drones as allies: drones attack mechs within their aggro radius, so they kill or weaken hunters; fighting near living drones, or not clearing them, may bank free points (their sim: 0.45 per match).",
  "Late-game ordering insight: the final circle closes to zero before the time cap, so the last deaths are zone deaths ordered by HP; max-HP upgrades and cubes decide that order, armor does not.",
  "Closest-approach bullet dodge and a lateral sidestep keyed on an enemy's visible laser-charging flag and aim yaw.",
  "Count walls, not trees, as cover: trees break sight but not shots and hunters keep a 5 s memory."
 ],

  "Gun lead is first-order constant velocity with no check that the lead point is clear, no handling of strafing reversals, and the fire gate is evaluated against a centre-height aim regardless of target vertical motion.",
